title: feat(security)!: retire the walled legacy platform-admin grant dual read and its deprecation log (#11663 L5)
body:
Fixes #18336

Clause-②: yes

Leg **L5** of the accepted #11663 platform-admin re-anchor design — the **EXIT** of the migration window L4 opened in 17.3.0. Under a **walled** tenancy posture (`group` / `isolated`), a legacy unscoped `admin_full_access` grant row no longer confers `PLATFORM_ADMIN`, and the once-per-process deprecation pointer that announced this retires with it.

## The ruling this is built against, and the two constraints it did not touch

The maintainer ruled option **B** on 2026-09-16 (`issuecomment-5695555178`): #11663's design governs over ADR-0131 D13 for these two symbols, and the card stays on the **17.x** line. ADR-0131 was amended accordingly on `origin/main` before this branch was cut — verified here, not inherited: commit `0b271e2e`, `docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md`, and the amended **D5** states the scope in its own words:

> The legacy unscoped anchor retires with D13 **for the `single` posture only**: its **walled** half, together with the two symbols that carry the migration window — `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` and `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` — **left D13 on 2026-09-16** and retire on the **17.x** line under #11663's design instead (#18336).

Two standing constraints the ruling did **not** touch, and which make the scope walled-only rather than all-postures:

> The rest of Choice 4A (#11974, 2026-08-25) stands: **retiring the walled write must not retire the `single` one**

(maintainer, 2026-09-08, #16682 comment `5587754690`)

> 比如临时启动的开发环境，我不可能去配置啊

(maintainer, 2026-09-16, the session that produced the ruling — the zero-config constraint)

⇒ The `single` posture keeps its zero-config first-user promotion **and** its grant row. Its disposition is #11979's (Choice 4B), out of scope here. The all-postures reading was measured on this card before dispatch and turns **11 pins red**; this branch does not take it, and the pin `an unscoped admin_full_access grant still confers PLATFORM_ADMIN with no config at all` is green and kept deliberately.

## What changed

**`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`**
- §6b: the legacy row-id route to `hasPlatformAdminGrant` is posture-keyed. A new `legacyGrantAnchorRetired = postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`, hoisted once beside the `unscopedUserPsIds` set, gates the one line that derives standing from an unscoped `admin_full_access` grant.
- The `else if (hasPlatformAdminGrant)` arm is **removed**. It carried one thing — the deprecation pointer — and the chain collapses to a bare `if (configConfersPlatformAdmin)`.

**`packages/core/src/security/platform-admin.ts` / `security/index.ts`**
- `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` and `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` are deleted, along with their once-per-process latch, and dropped from the re-export list.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`**
- The boot-side pointer call and the `sys_user` read that fed it are gone.
- ⭐ **The fail-closed backstop is no longer skipped when a legacy holder exists.** L4 skipped it on the stated ground that 「the deployment HAS an administrator, on the old anchor」 and that the pointer carried the remedy instead. Both premises die with the walled dual read: such a rig now has **zero** platform administrators. It is told, at `error`, naming the variable, the row and its holder.

## The boundary this card draws, stated because it is easy to read wider than it is

The retirement takes the **anchor**, not the **row** and not the **grant**. A walled holder keeps the `admin_full_access` permission set they hold — its name and everything downstream resolves from that name — and loses only platform-admin **standing**: the rung, the built-in `platform_admin` position, and every consumer of those. Nothing here writes, deletes or re-owns a grant row; that row's ownership is ADR-0131 **C3**'s, on the v18 line, and the amendment says the drop 「adds no NULL row, removes none, and re-owns none」. `packages/spec` is untouched (this lane's standing red line).

That boundary is **pinned**, not merely described: `the retirement takes the ANCHOR, not the GRANT — the held set still grants what it grants`. If a later leg widens to the row, that pin is the one to re-author deliberately.

## Evidence

**Clause-② confirmed on the rebuilt artefact**, not on source alone (`turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/plugin-security`, 18/18 tasks, exit 0):

| probe on `packages/core/dist` | `reportLegacy…` | `resetLegacy…` | positive control | negative control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| occurrences in `index.d.ts` | **0** | **0** | `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` 4, `setPlatformAdminConfigSink` 2 | — |
| `name in await import('index.js')` | **false** | **false** | both `true`, `typeof function` | `notAnExport_xyz` false |

⇒ two symbols leave a published entry. Breaking shape, graded `minor` under the launch-window convention, on `@objectstack/core` **and** `@objectstack/plugin-security`.

**Negative-pin dissolution.** Every negative pin this branch relies on was dissolved: the forbidden behaviour was put back on disk (anchor hit verified, blob hash before/after recorded), the suite was watched go red, and the restore was proven by `blob == HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD` — not by an exit code.

| pin family | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| walled rigs derive nothing from the legacy row | delete the `&& !legacyGrantAnchorRetired` gate | **5 failed / 26 passed** — the two walled-standing arms, the anchor-vs-grant boundary pin, the seeded-read arm, and the fourth-corner pin |
| the boot fail-closed line is no longer skipped | re-wrap the emission in `if (!unscopedHolder)` | **1 failed / 23 passed** — `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` |
| the symbol is gone from the module | add a stub `export function reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` to `platform-admin.ts` | **1 failed / 24 passed** — the module pin only; the entry pin stayed green |
| the symbol is gone from the published entry | add the export to `security/index.ts` | **1 failed / 24 passed** — the entry pin only; the module pin stayed green |

The last two are deliberately separate: each mutation reds exactly one of the two absence pins, which is what makes them two measurements rather than one restated twice.

⛔ Per the security family's disclosure discipline, the evidence above describes the consequence of a **proposed** mutation to this branch and carries no reproduction recipe for the shipped product.

**A measurement defect found and fixed in the suite's own double.** The pin `adds NO read: the recorded query multiset is identical under both answers of the gate` failed on first run, reporting a `sys_position` read whose `$in` differed by `platform_admin`. It was not a real difference: the resolver issues `{ name: { $in: grants.positions } }` — a live reference to an array §6c mutates **after** the query is issued — and the double stored `opts.where` by reference, so the comparison read the array's final contents instead of the query as issued. The double now deep-copies at record time, and the two postures are measured byte-identical. The same latent shape in a **sibling** harness is reported below as an out-of-scope finding.

**Tests and gates.** `pnpm typecheck` green for `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` (`VERDICT command-exit 0`). Targeted suites: `resolve-authz-context.platform-admin-config.test.ts` + `platform-admin.test.ts` **56 passed**, `bootstrap-platform-admin-walled-owner.test.ts` **24 passed**. Gate families were re-derived from the real diff with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths passed) and reconciled with `--ran`.

## Acceptance notes

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json` carries a clause describing the retired behaviour (「the once-per-process [authz] pointer names the OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL config line」) and names `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` in an anchor's parenthetical. It is **outside this dispatch's declared file surface**, so it is not touched here; the anchor symbol itself is `parsePlatformAdminEmails`, which still resolves. Noted for whoever owns the checklist.
- `PlatformAdminConfigSink.warn` now has no caller inside `@objectstack/core`. It is left in place deliberately: removing it would be a **third** published-surface removal, wider than this card, and it would break every consumer that passes an object literal with a `warn` member.
- ADR-0131's own text is untouched — it was amended for this leg by #18413 before this branch existed.

## Patch round 1 — the contract review's findings 1, 2 and 4

The at-tier review (`issuecomment-5737292414`) returned FAIL on one blocking finding and two cheap ones. All three are addressed in this branch; nothing that PASSED was touched.

### Finding 1 (blocking) — the retirement was done at one of the anchor's TWO readers

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts` enumerated platform administrators from the same unscoped, in-window `admin_full_access` row on **every** posture, while §6b had stopped deriving standing from it under a wall. One anchor, two readers, disagreeing — and the disagreement is introduced by this diff, so it is fixed here rather than sequenced.

Grade 1 of `resolveAdminUserIds` is now keyed on the identical expression the derivation site uses (`postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`), hoisted once per enumeration; under a wall the grade's `sys_permission_set` scan is skipped outright, so that path also issues one read fewer. `single` is untouched, and the two zero-population refusals gained a conditional clause naming `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, because 「restore the `admin_full_access` row」 stopped being a remedy that ends the emptiness on a walled rig.

Direction, stated because it reads backwards easily: under a wall the guard now refuses **more** (it protects the config-anchored administrator a write used to be allowed to take away) and refuses **wrongly** less (revoking the inert row is no longer reported as removing the last administrator). Both are narrowings toward the already-declared model.

**Walled coverage was as much the finding as the logic.** `last-admin-guard.config-anchor.test.ts` gains a seven-case `[#11663 L5]` suite that drives both walled postures and pairs every walled arm with a `single` control on the identical fixture. The two posture-blind sibling suites (`last-admin-guard.test.ts`, `last-admin-guard.re-pricing.test.ts`) now pin `single` explicitly instead of inheriting whatever the box exports, and the pre-L5 pin 「ALLOWS it when the same user also holds the legacy grant」 says `single` in its title.

Dissolution, both new pin families:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| remove the grade-1 posture gate | **2 failed / 16 passed** — the blocking arm fails with `promise resolved "{ id: 'usr_owner', … email_verified: false }" instead of rejecting`, i.e. the write that ends the last config-anchored standing goes through; the inverse arm fails with it. Every `single` control stayed green. |
| force the walled remedy clause empty | **1 failed / 17 passed** — only the remedy arm; the refusal itself fired unchanged, which is what makes the clause additive and conditional rather than a new verdict. |

### Finding 2 — the ② naming gap

Closed by naming, not by stating a precedent. `packages/runtime/src/index.ts:247` and `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts:4` are `export * from '@objectstack/core'` (re-verified here; a repo-wide grep finds exactly those two), so the two removed names leave those published surfaces too. Both are now in the changeset, alongside `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, whose behaviour this round changes. The level is unaffected — all publishable packages sit in one `fixed` group — and the reason for naming them is the CHANGELOG tombstone an upgrading consumer of *those* packages greps. This follows the `ApiRegistry` precedent rather than the core-only one.

### Finding 4 — prose

`admin-standing-surface.ts`'s `sys_user_permission_set` reason is posture-qualified, and so is the module header's account of where `hasPlatformAdminGrant` comes from. ⚠️ The first attempt cited the tracker ids and `check:doc-authoring` refused it — that `reason` is a runtime string that reaches customers, and the baseline is shrink-only. The sentence now says the same thing without them.

### Finding 3

Not touched here, by instruction — the seat filed it separately as #19145.

<sub>⚠️ This section was appended by the `domain:services` seat, ⛔ not by the delivering dev: the dev writes a PR body once at creation and never PATCHes it, so it handed the text over in its report. The seat verified the load-bearing claims against the tree before appending — the guard is posture-keyed at `last-admin-guard.ts:941` (control on `origin/main`: 0 occurrences) and the changeset names all five packages — and ⛔ did not verify every figure quoted above, which is the next reviewer's to test.</sub>

## Patch round 2 — the last unkeyed reader of the anchor

The at-tier review of `61a951c97` (`issuecomment-5737610351`) returned FAIL on one blocking finding: the retirement was still done at only some of the anchor's readers. This round closes the class rather than one instance.

### The reader set, re-measured here and now closed

#11663's design P3 enumerates the in-repo consumers of 「who are the platform admins?」. Their state on this head, each verified in this branch rather than inherited:

| reader | how it answers | state |
|---|---|---|
| `resolve-authz-context.ts` §6b | derives | keyed (round 0) |
| `plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` | reads the row at boot | keyed (round 0) |
| `plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts` | counts the population | keyed (round 1) |
| `plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts` | **consumes the verdict** | ✅ needs nothing |
| `plugin-auth/src/ensure-default-organization.ts` | **confers** on the population | keyed (**this round**) |

`explain-engine.ts` was checked, not assumed: at `:562` it sets `hasPlatformAdminGrant: grants.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'`, reading the resolver's one verdict back, and its only `sys_user_permission_set` read is `collectGrantProvenance`, which reports *why grants were dropped* and derives no standing. It moved with §6b in round 0.

**An independent sweep says the set is closed.** A grep for source reads of an *unscoped* `admin_full_access` grant (`organization_id: null` beside the admin permission set, non-test) returns exactly two files in the whole tree — `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` and `ensure-default-organization.ts` — both now keyed. The remaining files that merely name `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS` were read: a config-validation refusal, the spec declaration, the seeded set definition, a CLI formatter, sandbox type assertions, and the two already-keyed derivation sites.

### What changed

**`ensureDefaultOrganization` step 2** — its legacy fallback is keyed on the same expression the derivation uses. This reader is worse than the guard: the guard *counted* a holder, this one **confers** — it writes the account it picks a `sys_member { role: 'owner' }` row on the Default Organization and hands them the org's seeded rows through `claimSeedOwnership`. Unkeyed, a walled rig carrying a legacy row bound, as an organization owner, an account the derivation grades `MEMBER` and the bootstrap logs at `error` as non-existent. Reachable despite plugin-auth skipping the helper under a wall (`auth-plugin.ts:1100`), because `@objectstack/organizations` — which a walled posture requires — wraps and calls it.

Under a wall with no verified declared owner, the answer is now `no_admin`: **a wait, not a silent mis-binding.** The declared owner's verifying update re-runs the helper through the trigger predicate, and the binding happens then.

**The trigger predicate's grant-insert arm** retires with it under a wall — cost only, since the helper answered `no_admin` from that grant either way. ⛔ The `sys_user` arms are deliberately untouched: on a walled rig the declared owner's verifying update is the only write that ever grows the population, so keying that off would strand the deployment forever. The sibling predicate `shouldReplayBootstrapFor` in `plugin-security` already spells the same walled exclusion.

**Coverage.** `ensure-default-organization.test.ts` had 0 posture-env sites; it now pins `single` for the whole file instead of inheriting the ambient environment, and gains a seven-case `[#11663 L5]` walled suite in which every walled arm is paired with a `single` control on the identical fixture — including the zero-config default (both tenancy inputs unset), a no-added-read pin, and the config anchor still binding under a wall.

Dissolution of the two new pin families:

| mutation | suite | result |
|---|---|---|
| remove the step-2 posture gate | `ensure-default-organization.test.ts` | **3 failed / 38 passed** — the walled binding arm fails with `expected { defaultOrgCreated: true, … } to match object { defaultOrgCreated: false, … }`, i.e. the organization really is created and the legacy holder really is bound; the unverified-owner wait and the no-added-read pin fail with it. Every `single` control stayed green. |
| the same mutation | `walled-default-org-self-registrant.pin.test.ts` | **1 failed / 4 passed** — the re-authored pin, and only it. The surviving positive control stayed green, so the inverted assertion is falsifiable rather than vacuous. |
| delete the trigger's walled exclusion | `ensure-default-organization.test.ts` | **1 failed / 40 passed** — only the trigger arm; the helper's own answers were untouched, which is what makes it a cost fix and not a verdict change. |

### The one declared out-of-lane change

`packages/plugins/organizations/src/walled-default-org-self-registrant.pin.test.ts` pinned the pre-L5 model: its positive control asserted that under `isolated` a legacy grant still anchors the bootstrap, saying in its own words that the negative cases were 「green only because objectstack#11211 stopped minting that row on a walled box, not because this path is inert」. This diff makes that path inert, so the pin is **inverted rather than deleted** — the fixture is cloud#1509's reported shape and it is the only place in the tree that pins what a walled rig does with a legacy row at this seam. The suite's method survives: the operator case above it (a declared address reading verified) carries the positive-control role, and the header now records that clause 2 rests on the keying rather than on what gets minted.

⚠️ `packages/plugins/organizations` is **not** in this lane's named package set. This is a deliberate, declared, **test-only** widening forced by CI — its runtime source is untouched.

### Changeset

`@objectstack/organizations` is added at `minor`. ⛔ Not because a test was re-authored — that earns nothing. It is named because the behaviour an operator gets *from that package* moves: it is the runtime that performs the default-organization bootstrap on a walled deployment, and after this change it no longer creates a Default Organization for a legacy grant holder, nor binds them as its owner. The tombstone belongs in the CHANGELOG of the package whose behaviour changed, which is the same reasoning that named `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` in round 1.

### One thing named rather than left to be found

`plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts:1402` decides its override actor with `posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN' || perms.includes(ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS)`. Its first arm moved with §6b in round 0; its second reads the permission-set NAME, which a walled legacy holder still carries — the declared 「the retirement takes the ANCHOR, not the GRANT」 boundary this PR pins. ⚠️ Measured: this diff does **not** change that function's answer for such an account (before, both arms were true; after, the second still is), so it is not a dual-track this PR opens and it is not fixed here. It belongs to whatever leg disposes of the row itself — ADR-0131 C3 on the v18 line, and #11979 for `single`.

<sub>⚠️ Appended by the `domain:services` seat, ⛔ not by the delivering dev, which writes a body once at creation and never PATCHes it. The seat independently re-ran the closure sweep with a **different, cruder** instrument (file-level co-occurrence of the token with an `organization_id: null` spelling) and reached the same conclusion by a different route: its extra hits — `sys-user-position.object.ts`, `runtime/src/security/actor-user.ts`, `spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts` — were each read and are a refusal's explanatory comment, a docstring example, and the spec's own constant declaration. ⛔ None derives the population. The seat also verified the surface (16 files, nothing outside the authorised set, zero `packages/spec`, the `organizations` touch test-only). The dissolution figures above are the dev's and are the next reviewer's to test.</sub>
